dae498ec13ecb33364d0afa7693879b09e5e47d2.summary: ElvenPath reported on the N40 banking trojan, used in a recent campaign against Chilean banks. It is described as an evolved version of a Brazilian banking trojan used in earlier attacks. The malware relies on DLL Hijacking: a legitimate Windows application is dropped with a renamed trojan DLL signed using a black-market certificate, so SmartScreen only sees a legitimate app run. It also uses real-time string decoding, non-standard ports for command and control, and can steal credentials and replace a bitcoin wallet in the victim's clipboard. The report does not say how N40 spreads.…
